decisions.reason: The candidate uses the symptom log and contrast probe correctly: the tab is claimed/titled but meta.status stays 'none', file-trace's own RPC reads the same file fine, so the fault is localized to the workspace-files resource-provider/RPC metadata delivery chain rather than disk or the external plugin renderer. It also notes static serving (62/62) does not prove activation, consistent with the declared host row.

Correctly distinguishes the valid per-module 62/62 sweep from the invalid all-in-one ~4-5 KB join 404, explains the real loader partitions requests under a ~3 KB URL cap, and states the oversized join must never be cited as 'modules missing'. The 60 vs 62 roster/probe discrepancy is not addressed, but the rubric only requires evidence-bounded treatment, and the core probe discipline is fully correct.

The fold warnings are correctly separated as an unrelated warning family (the invented END-marker/fix-version detail is permitted extra, not penalized). However, the report entirely omits the boot-manifest-based analysis of textpreview→documentpreview and the new session-only canOpen scope, so it never explains the outside/absolute-address claim failure versus the session tab's stalled metadata.

Gives the correct order: one host restart (citing the alpha.1 self-heal), then rollback to the verified 0.1.3-alpha.2 escape hatch, then upstream reporting, and explicitly rejects plugin-side rewrite/retry/fallback. It implicitly treats the alpha.1 roster mismatch as prior art by ruling out 'missing bytes' via the 62/62 sweep. Proposed actions suffice.

The upstream package includes the per-module sweep, contrast reader, roster excerpt and invalid-join caveat, but omits versions/profile upgrade history, the exact session vs absolute addresses, and meta.status. The fail-loud proposal is only a roster-vs-served-bytes check, which the criterion explicitly notes is insufficient by itself; no provider-registration or metadata-RPC readiness diagnostic is proposed.

caps.reason: The report explicitly states the joined-URL 404 must never be cited as 'modules missing' and uses the 62/62 sweep to rule out missing bytes.
The report explicitly rejects plugin-side rewrite, retry, fallback and any repair of the service; mitigation is host restart, rollback, and upstream report.
